newsitem.title: USA: Republicans urged to keep quiet on Gingrich.
newsitem.headline: Republicans urged to keep quiet on Gingrich.

text.p: With House Speaker Newt Gingrich's ethics problems mounting, House Republican leaders urged their colleagues to keep quiet until they hear his side of the story, according to a letter released Friday.

The notice faxed to House Republicans around the country was to quell the type of comments heard Thursday when two Republicans said Gingrich owed them a full explanation before they are asked to vote Jan. 7 to re-elect him as speaker.

Their comments came after Gingrich's attorney Jan Baran said he would no longer represent him before the ethics committee, apparently due to a dispute over the accuracy of information given to congressional investigators.

"On behalf of Newt, I am asking all members to please defer comment on this matter until there is an official statement from the Committee on Standards of Official Conduct and until you have heard Newt's response to any information issued by the committee," Republican Conference Chairman John Boehner of Indiana wrote.
Boehner promised that Gingrich would immediately contact the legislators after the ethics committee issues a statement or releases a report.
The ethics case had been expected to be wrapped up before the opening of the new Congress but Gingrich's sudden switch in attorneys could prolong the inquiry.

In September the four-member ethics subcommittee began looking into whether Gingrich provided "accurate, reliable and complete information" about his college course or a tax-free foundation "in the course of communicating with the committee, either directly or through counsel."

This issue was added to the broader ongoing inquiry into whether Gingrich broke federal tax laws barring use of tax-exempt charities for partisan political purposes in the college course he taught. Once the panel gives Gingrich a statement of findings, he will have 30 days to respond.

In a joint announcement issued late Thursday "to avoid a growing misperception," Gingrich's press secretary Tony Blankley and Baran confirmed that Baran and his law firm "are no longer representing him directly before the ethics committee or its special counsel."
Baran said his firm did not submit any information to the ethics committee without Gingrich's prior review and approval, and he believed this was also the committee's view.
Rep. John Linder, R-Georgia, a Gingrich confidant, told a reporter that Gingrich had in fact signed an erroneous statement but that the error had been made by Baran.
After this information was made public Republican Rep. Peter King of New York said Gingrich should give a detailed explanation "as soon as possible prior to Jan. 7."
Another Republican, Rep. Christopher Shays of Connecticut, reiterated that if the ethics report was not released before the speakership vote, he would abstain.
